svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The endocrine system: glands secrete hormones directly into the blood."], [1, "The hypothalamus and pituitary control many other glands."], [4, "The pituitary releases TSH, which travels in the blood to the thyroid; the thyroid releases thyroxine."], [8, "The pancreas secretes insulin into the blood; its target organs include the liver and muscles."], [11.5, "In danger the adrenal glands release adrenaline: the heart beats faster."], [14.5, "Each hormone affects only target cells that have receptors for it."]]
svg.title: The endocrine system
svg.desc: The main endocrine glands in the body (hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal glands, pancreas, ovaries and testes) with hormones carried in the blood to their target organs.
svg.text: Positions approximate. Both ovaries (female) and testes (male) are shown.

g.data-info: Links the nervous and endocrine systems. Controls the pituitary; makes ADH.
The "master gland": releases TSH, FSH, LH, growth hormone and ADH, many of which control other glands.
Secretes melatonin, which helps control sleep (circadian rhythm).
Secretes thyroxine, which controls the metabolic rate. Needs iodine.
On top of the kidneys. Secrete adrenaline in the fight-or-flight response.
Islets of Langerhans secrete insulin and glucagon, which control blood glucose.
Ovaries secrete oestrogen and progesterone; testes secrete testosterone.
Hormones are carried in the plasma to target organs, whose cells have receptors for them. Effects are slower and longer-lasting than nerve impulses.
g.text: Pituitary · TSH, FSH, LH, ADH, growth hormone
Pancreas · insulin and glucagon: blood glucose
Adrenal glands · adrenaline: fight or flight
Hypothalamus · controls the pituitary; makes ADH
